summary: net: stmmac: protect updates of 64-bit statistics counters
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: stmmac: protect updates of 64-bit statistics counters

As explained by a comment in <linux/u64_stats_sync.h>, write side of struct
u64_stats_sync must ensure mutual exclusion, or one seqcount update could
be lost on 32-bit platforms, thus blocking readers forever. Such lockups
have been observed in real world after stmmac_xmit() on one CPU raced with
stmmac_napi_poll_tx() on another CPU.

To fix the issue without introducing a new lock, split the statics into
three parts:

1. fields updated only under the tx queue lock,
2. fields updated only during NAPI poll,
3. fields updated only from interrupt context,

Updates to fields in the first two groups are already serialized through
other locks. It is sufficient to split the existing struct u64_stats_sync
so that each group has its own.

Note that tx_set_ic_bit is updated from both contexts. Split this counter
so that each context gets its own, and calculate their sum to get the total
value in stmmac_get_ethtool_stats().

For the third group, multiple interrupts may be processed by different CPUs
at the same time, but interrupts on the same CPU will not nest. Move fields
from this group to a newly created per-cpu struct stmmac_pcpu_stats.

summary: interconnect: Don't access req_list while it's being manipulated
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

interconnect: Don't access req_list while it's being manipulated

The icc_lock mutex was split into separate icc_lock and icc_bw_lock
mutexes in [1] to avoid lockdep splats. However, this didn't adequately
protect access to icc_node::req_list.

The icc_set_bw() function will eventually iterate over req_list while
only holding icc_bw_lock, but req_list can be modified while only
holding icc_lock. This causes races between icc_set_bw(), of_icc_get(),
and icc_put().

Example A:

  CPU0                               CPU1
  ----                               ----
  icc_set_bw(path_a)
    mutex_lock(&icc_bw_lock);
                                     icc_put(path_b)
                                       mutex_lock(&icc_lock);
    aggregate_requests()
      hlist_for_each_entry(r, ...
                                       hlist_del(...
        <r = invalid pointer>

Example B:

  CPU0                               CPU1
  ----                               ----
  icc_set_bw(path_a)
    mutex_lock(&icc_bw_lock);
                                     path_b = of_icc_get()
                                       of_icc_get_by_index()
                                         mutex_lock(&icc_lock);
                                         path_find()
                                           path_init()
    aggregate_requests()
      hlist_for_each_entry(r, ...
                                             hlist_add_head(...
        <r = invalid pointer>

Fix this by ensuring icc_bw_lock is always held before manipulating
icc_node::req_list. The additional places icc_bw_lock is held don't
perform any memory allocations, so we should still be safe from the
original lockdep splats that motivated the separate locks.

[1] commit af42269c3523 ("interconnect: Fix locking for runpm vs reclaim")

summary: drm/msm: RCU-free the scheduler-containing ring and VM objects
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/msm: RCU-free the scheduler-containing ring and VM objects

Both struct msm_ringbuffer and struct msm_gem_vm embed a struct
drm_gpu_scheduler.  msm_ringbuffer_destroy() and the VM free callback
msm_gem_vm_free() call drm_sched_fini() on the embedded scheduler and then
free the containing object with plain kfree().

drm_sched_fence_get_timeline_name() returns fence->sched->name, and the
scheduler fence keeps a .release callback so it is not ops-detached on
signalling.  A finished fence exported to userspace (the submit out-fence, or
a VM_BIND fence, via sync_file / drm_syncobj) keeps pointing at the embedded
scheduler after the ring/VM is freed, so a later get_timeline_name() --
reachable unprivileged through SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO -- dereferences freed slab
memory (KASAN slab-use-after-free read).

Per the dma-fence lifetime contract the exporter must keep the data backing a
signalled fence alive for an RCU grace period.  Free the scheduler-containing
objects with kfree_rcu() instead of kfree().

Patchwork: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/750234/

summary: ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic

parse_sec_desc() constructs SID and DACL pointers by adding untrusted
32-bit offsets to the security descriptor before checking their bounds.
The existing checks reject offsets into the descriptor header, but do
not reject offsets beyond the descriptor's length.

On a 32-bit kernel, a large offset can wrap the pointer before the
descriptor. The end-only checks in parse_sid() and parse_dacl() can then
accept it, allowing an authenticated SMB2 SET_INFO request to access
memory outside the security descriptor and fault the kernel.

Check each nonzero offset against acl_len before constructing its
pointer. Initialize the optional owner and group SID pointers to NULL
so an omitted SID remains absent when parsing the DACL.

summary: media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path

hackrf_alloc_urbs() frees the URBs it allocated so far when one
allocation fails, but leaves the entries in dev->urb_list[] and
dev->urbs_initialized untouched. The caller, hackrf_start_streaming(),
then calls hackrf_free_urbs() on the error path, which walks
dev->urbs_initialized entries and calls usb_free_urb() a second time on
the already-freed URBs, causing a use-after-free (slab-use-after-free
Write in usb_free_urb()).

Drop the redundant cleanup loop inside hackrf_alloc_urbs() and let
hackrf_free_urbs(), which the caller already invokes on error, own the
cleanup of the successfully allocated URBs.

summary: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners

mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listener directly
instead of going through mptcp_listen(). It consequently misses setting
SOCK_RCU_FREE on the parent MPTCP socket.

tcp_child_process() can invoke the listener's subflow_data_ready()
callback without holding the MPTCP parent lock or a reference to the
parent. An authenticated MP_JOIN racing with endpoint teardown can
therefore access the parent after its last reference has been dropped.
The ADD_ADDR error path can also close an already published listener.

Set SOCK_RCU_FREE before __inet_listen_sk() publishes the TCP listener,
matching mptcp_listen(). This protects the parent on every subsequent
close path, including a failed endpoint addition.

summary: nfsd: don't modify a session slot when replaying its cached reply
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: don't modify a session slot when replaying its cached reply

nfsd4_sequence() claims a session slot by setting NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE
under nn->client_lock. A reply served from the slot's reply cache does
not claim it, and that distinction lived only in cstate->status, which
nfsd4_sequence() set to nfserr_replay_cache. Commit cc028a10a48c
("NFSD: Hoist status code encoding into XDR encoder functions") moved
nfsd4_proc_compound()'s cstate->status assignment below the out:
label, and the replay path's goto out was the one path that relied on
skipping it. The test in nfsd4_sequence_done() therefore no longer
identifies a replay, and every replay now stores its reply and clears
NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE as though it owned the slot.

NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE is the interlock: check_slot_seqid() rejects every
sequence id for a slot that is in use, before replay_matches_cache()
runs. A replay never sets it, so two replays can be in flight on the
same slot at once. One can read slot->sl_cred under nn->client_lock
while the other's completion frees and rebuilds it from the XDR
encoder without that lock. Two completions can also collide with each
other and release the same group_info twice. free_svc_cred() leaves
cr_uid, cr_gid and cr_flavor intact, so the reader passes every
earlier test in same_creds() and dereferences a NULL cr_group_info.
From a 6.12.91 production server:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000004
  CPU: 63 UID: 0 PID: 39015 Comm: nfsd
  RIP: 0010:same_creds+0x38/0xa0 [nfsd]
  RDX: 0000000000000000
  Call Trace:
   nfsd4_sequence+0x6a8/0x910 [nfsd]
   nfsd4_proc_compound+0x345/0x670 [nfsd]
   nfsd_dispatch+0x100/0x220 [nfsd]
   svc_process_common+0x311/0x700 [sunrpc]
   svc_process+0x131/0x1c0 [sunrpc]
   svc_recv+0x7ef/0x9c0 [sunrpc]
   nfsd+0xa3/0x100 [nfsd]
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Since v6.14 a live session's slot table can shrink, and the unowned
store becomes a use-after-free write. nfsd4_sequence() defers the
shrink while a slot is in use, but it tests NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE, which a
replay does not set, so free_session_slots() can kfree() the slot the
replay still holds in cstate->slot.

Record the claim in cstate->slot_owned when nfsd4_sequence() accepts a
request and test that in nfsd4_sequence_done(), so only the request
that claimed the slot updates its cached reply and clears
NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE. svc_generic_init_request() zeroes the compound
response before each request, so the flag starts clear.

summary: HID: roccat: kovaplus: reject short button reports
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: roccat: kovaplus: reject short button reports

The raw event callback runs before HID core validates and zero-pads the
report.  It passes the buffer to helpers which inspect data[0] and read a
complete struct kovaplus_mouse_report_button for button reports.  A
truncated report can therefore cause an out-of-bounds read.

Require enough data for the button report before calling either helper.
Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init
sequence") added the same kind of raw-event length validation to hid-asus.

summary: assoc_array: don't chain a new shortcut onto an existing one
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

assoc_array: don't chain a new shortcut onto an existing one

When a full node's leaves and the new key all share the node's segment,
assoc_array_insert_into_terminal_node() replaces the node with a
shortcut to a pair of new nodes.  If the node is itself the target of a
shortcut, the new shortcut is installed as that shortcut's next node,
and a shortcut leading to a shortcut is something nothing expects:
assoc_array_walk() indexes the second one as a node, and
assoc_array_apply_edit() hits the BUG_ON() in the loop that adjusts
nr_leaves_on_branch, on that same insertion.

Deletion gets a node there.  When the subtree below a shortcut shrinks
enough, assoc_array_delete() collapses it into one node below the
shortcut, and the leaves it collects can all share that node's segment.
The next key that shares it too takes this path.  Eighteen insertions
and a deletion are enough: sixteen keys that agree on bits 0-11, one
that leaves them at bit 8 and is deleted again, and one more that agrees
with the sixteen.

Have the new shortcut replace the one in front of the node as well.
assoc_array_insert_shortcut() gives it that shortcut's back pointer and
parent slot, so the caller installs it where that one was, and excises
the old shortcut along with the node, which takes a second entry in
excised_meta[].  The new shortcut's index key comes from the new key up
to the new skip level, so it covers what the old one did.

Found by a userspace test doing random insertions and deletions on keys
that share long prefixes; a targeted case builds a shortcut, deletes
down to the collapse and inserts one more key.

summary: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering

userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pending missing faults before clearing the
VMA's userfaultfd registration. With per-VMA fault locking, holding
mmap_lock for write does not prevent another fault from queuing after
the wakeup but before userfaultfd_clear_vma() write-locks the VMA. That
waiter can then remain asleep indefinitely.

Call vma_start_write() before waking waiters. Existing fault handlers
queue themselves before dropping the VMA read lock, and new readers are
excluded until mmap_write_unlock().

summary: xfrm: retry inexact policy lookup after node reinsertion
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: retry inexact policy lookup after node reinsertion

An inexact policy lookup first records pointers to candidate hlist heads
and then traverses the lists.  A concurrent policy insertion can merge
inexact tree nodes between those operations:

  lookup                         policy insertion
  ------                         ----------------
  find inexact candidates
    save obsolete hlist head
                                 write_seqcount_begin(&bin->count)
                                 merge inexact tree nodes
                                   hlist_del_rcu(&policy->bydst)
                                   reinsert policy->bydst in survivor
                                 write_seqcount_end(&bin->count)
  evaluate saved candidate list
    miss the moved policy

The merge immediately reinserts the same hlist node into the surviving
tree node.  RCU keeps the policy alive, but it does not provide a
consistent view while its list node is moved.  A lookup that selected the
obsolete list can observe it empty.  A lookup already traversing a moved
policy can instead follow the next pointer rewritten by the reinsertion.
Either case can return an incorrect IPsec policy result.

The per-bin sequence counter already brackets calls to
xfrm_policy_inexact_insert_node(), including node merges.  The read side,
however, currently validates the counter only while searching an
individual rb-tree.  A successful search returns without validation, and
the later candidate-list traversal is outside that read-side section.

Snapshot the per-bin sequence before discovering candidate heads and
validate it after evaluating all candidate lists.   Retry the lookup if
the inexact policy tree changes while it is being searched.

summary: lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked

nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked
under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). The nlm_blocked list
reference is all that keeps the block alive across that window.
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() does take one of its own, but not until after
the lock has been dropped. Unmounting the nfsd filesystem while a lock
request is still blocked reaches nlmsvc_traverse_blocks(), which drops
the list reference and frees the block along with the nlm_rqst hanging
off it.

  Read of size 8 at addr ffff88811b04c808 by task lockd/8377
    nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230
    nlmsvc_retry_blocked+0x61c/0x800
    lockd+0x144/0x1c0
  Freed by task 8392:
    nlmsvc_release_block+0x231/0x290
    nlmsvc_traverse_blocks+0x139/0x1b0
    nlm_traverse_files+0x1aa/0xa00
    nlmsvc_free_host_resources+0x12/0x60
    nlm_shutdown_hosts_net+0x127/0x280

Take a reference before releasing nlm_blocked_lock and drop it once
the retry has run.

summary: namespace: check a recursive bind mount for mount namespace loops
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

namespace: check a recursive bind mount for mount namespace loops

do_loopback() refuses to bind mount the file of a mount namespace that
is as old as the caller's or older because a mount namespace that holds
a mount of its own file, or of an ancestor's, would cause a cycle. But
it only checks the dentry the bind mount starts from. With MS_REC
everything below it is copied and do_loopback() passes
CL_COPY_MNT_NS_FILE so mount namespace files below the source are
copied.

That's fine for a source in the caller's own mount namespace. Every
mount namespace file in there passed the same check when it was
bind-mounted. It isn't fine for a source in another mount namespace.
may_copy_tree() accepts a bind mount of any nsfs or pidfs file no matter
what mount namespace it lives in so that /proc/<pid>/ns/<ns> and pidfds
can be bind mounted. If we create a bind-mount stack of mount namespaces
file descriptors the kernel will copy them irrespective of their
ancestoral relationship to the mount namespace in question:

  151 146 0:7 net:[4026531833] /tmp/nrc/y rw - nsfs nsfs rw
  152 151 0:7 mnt:[4026532293] /tmp/nrc/y rw - nsfs nsfs rw

4026532293 inside mount namespace 4026532293. That namespace and every

namespace that stacks the file and repeating it leaks without limit:

  after control: Shmem:               380 kB
  child: mount(/proc/self/fd/6, MS_BIND|MS_REC): ok
  after cycle: Shmem:             65916 kB

summary: KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit)
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit)

When potentially reusing a shadow page, zap the shadow page if its number
of parent PTEs exceeds KVM's (mostly) arbitrary rmap recycling threshold.
Letting the guest create a (mostly) unbounded number of parent PTEs allows
the guest to coerce KVM into creating lists containing millions of PTEs,
effectively bounded only by the maximum number of shadow pages.

Because PTE lists are simple singly linked lists, removal is O(n).  Even
worse, if a list is constructed just so, teardown can be O(n^2), e.g. if
SPTEs are built such that zapping child SPTEs always zaps the last entry
in the list.  To cap things off, all paths that walk PTE lists do so
while holding mmu_lock, without conditionally rescheduling.

Using a doubly linked list would not address the issue, as removal would
remain O(n) since KVM still wouldn't know where in the list to remove from.
Removal could be made O(1) by storing a per-SPTE pointer, but that would
largely defeat the purpose of reusing SPs, and would penalize well-behaved
guests, especially for nested TDP where aliasing page tables is uncommon.

So, cap the maximum number of parent PTEs at the rmap limit.  In practice,
well-behaved guests will likely never run afoul of the limit.  E.g. when
running Linux as L1 with TDP, the number of parent PTEs for a single SP
tops out at under 200 (though undoubtedly obscure workloads can push it
higher).  Deliberately use a "greater than or equal" as opposed to rmap's
strictly "greater than", as the rmap code checks the threshold immediately
*after* inserting into the list, i.e. the limit is 1000 for rmaps, KVM just
very briefly blows past it.

Apply the check to both indirect and direct SPs, because while a fully
direct MMU naturally limits the number of parent PTEs to '1', direct SPs in
indirect MMUs have no such constraint.  E.g. if the guest maps a huge PTE
into many locations in its page tables, and KVM is backing the hugepage
with a direct SP, i.e. with a series of smaller pages, then KVM could end
up with a direct SP with many parents.

Note, shadow_mmu_try_split_huge_pages() always restarts the rmap walk or
bails entirely if it gets to the point where it tries to grab a SP, i.e.
there is *no* pre-existing bug that would be tripped by zapping a SP and
thus rmaps when getting a SP.

summary: ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs

usx2y_urb_capt_retire() wraps the ring buffer once per packet and
usx2y_urb_play_prepare() once per URB of nr_of_packs() packets of up to
50 frames. Both assume that the data fits in the buffer, and the hw
constraints only require about two 1 ms periods, so a packet larger
than the buffer on capture, or a URB larger than the buffer on playback,
violates that assumption.

Constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE in snd_usx2y_pcm_open() to at
least two URBs, 2 * nr_of_packs() * 50 frames, for both directions. The
bound is in frames and derived from the driver's own packet limit, so it
does not read the endpoint, whose altsetting is only selected in
prepare. Two URBs rather than one, because the position advances by a
URB on playback and only moves when a URB is less than the whole buffer.
Keep a guard in usx2y_urb_capt_retire() that drops a packet larger than
the buffer, for the case the constraint makes unreachable.

With nrpacks above about 163 (S16_LE) or 109 (S24_3LE) the bound exceeds
the 64 KiB buffer the substream preallocates (twice that with the
preallocation raised to its 128 KiB maximum), so hw_params fails for
those module settings. That is intended: the driver cannot be safe with
a URB larger than half the largest buffer.

Reproduced on 7.3-rc7 with a USB/IP device presenting the US-122
interface layout and 1024-byte packets into a 512-byte capture buffer:

  BUG: KASAN: out-of-bounds in i_usx2y_urb_complete+0x1285/0x1ac0
  Read of size 18446744073709551104 at addr ffff88800e448800 by task vhci_rx/83

Tested on 7.3-rc7 with the same device, S16_LE at 44100 Hz, nrpacks 4,
so the bound is 400 frames. A 128-frame capture buffer and a 200-frame
playback buffer are refused at hw_params with EINVAL. A 400-frame buffer
streams for 30 s in each direction with the position advancing inside
the buffer and no KASAN report; the capture guard did not fire. The
same 400-frame capture buffer with S24_3LE, which selects altsetting 2
in prepare, streams for 30 s with the same result.

summary: inet: frags: limit the truesize of a reassembly queue
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: frags: limit the truesize of a reassembly queue

The truesize of fragments in a reassembly queue is only bounded by
the per netns ipfrag_high_thresh sysctl, which has no upper limit.

inet_frag_reasm_finish() sums the truesize of all fragments in an int.
If this sum reaches 2^32, it wraps, and the final sk_wmem_alloc
adjustment of the socket owning the reassembled skb can cancel its own
reference, leading to a use-after-free of this socket.

This can be triggered from an unprivileged user/network namespace,
raising ipfrag_high_thresh and using padded TUN packets, which keep
a large truesize after being trimmed by ip_rcv_core().

Track the sum of the truesize of fragments in each queue, and refuse
a fragment that would make it bigger than INT_MAX / 2. Callers kill
the queue on this error. This bound is far above the needs of
legitimate traffic.

summary: media: microchip-csi2dc: fix async notifier leak on probe error path
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: microchip-csi2dc: fix async notifier leak on probe error path

csi2dc_of_parse() ends up calling csi2dc_prepare_notifier(), which
registers the V4L2 async notifier with v4l2_async_nf_register(). The
probe error label csi2dc_probe_cleanup_notifier is reached after
csi2dc_of_parse() has already succeeded (e.g. when media entity init,
csi2dc_power() or v4l2_async_register_subdev() fail), but it calls only
v4l2_async_nf_cleanup() and never v4l2_async_nf_unregister().

The notifier therefore stays chained in the global notifier_list while
the enclosing struct csi2dc_device is freed, leading to list corruption
and a use-after-free when the list is next walked.

Unregister the notifier before cleaning it up on the error path,
matching the teardown already done in csi2dc_remove().

summary: klist: avoid accesses after waking klist_remove()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

klist: avoid accesses after waking klist_remove()

klist_remove() waits until a node is unreferenced so that its caller can
free the containing object.  klist_release() currently publishes
waiter->woken and wakes the waiter before its final accesses to the waiter
and node.  klist_remove() can then return, allowing its stack waiter and
the containing object to be freed or reused while klist_release() is still
running.  In particular, bus_remove_driver() can free drv->p while
__device_attach() walks the same bus klist with bus_for_each_drv().

On an arm64 Cortex-A72 system, an unpatched 7.2.0-rc3 kernel with
CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT=y and CONFIG_KASAN=y reproduced the bug through the
in-tree I2C/at24 path.  KASAN reported a use-after-free in
klist_dec_and_del() reached from klist_next()/bus_for_each_drv() while
at24 was being unregistered.

Clear n_klist and take a task reference before publishing woken.  Use
release/acquire accesses for that publication and wake the referenced
task.  The task reference keeps the waiter task alive if it returns and
exits before wake_up_process().

summary: HID: multitouch: stop the release timer from being rearmed on remove
scsi: dc395x: sync the waiting_timer before freeing the host
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: dc395x: sync the waiting_timer before freeing the host

The waiting_timer callback re-arms itself and takes the host lock.
adapter_uninit() currently stops it with timer_delete(), which does not
wait for a callback already running on another CPU. The final
scsi_host_put() that frees the host (and the host lock the callback
dereferences) runs right after adapter_uninit(), so a concurrent or just
re-armed callback can fire after the free, leaving a potential
use-after-free window.

Replace timer_delete() with timer_shutdown_sync() at the top of
adapter_uninit(), before the host-lock section: the timer is dequeued,
a running callback is waited for and rearming is blocked before the chip
is halted, so it cannot fire at all once the adapter has ceased to
function. Waiting outside the lock avoids the self-deadlock that would
result from syncing a callback blocked on the lock we still hold.

No shutdown is needed for selto_timer because it has no reachable armer
or callback.

This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

summary: vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables

In __vringh_iov(), the F_INDIRECT branch descends into the indirect
table and continues before the descriptor accounting runs. A top-level
indirect descriptor is therefore never charged to count. If such a
descriptor sets NEXT to point back at itself, returning from the
indirect table resumes at the same top-level descriptor, which is again
not counted, so the walk never makes forward progress.

Because count stays flat and indirect_count is reset to 0 on every
return to the top-level table, neither bound in the loop check trips.
A guest can spin the vringh worker at 100% CPU inside __vringh_iov(),
an uninterruptible host DoS.

Move the descriptor accounting above the indirect switch so that a
top-level indirect descriptor is charged one top-level traversal step
before the walk descends into its table, bringing this re-entry under
the existing vrh->vring.num bound. Each top-level descriptor is still
charged at most one step and indirect_count still bounds a single
table, so legitimate chains (including the multiple-indirect case in
tools/virtio/vringh_test.c) stay within vring.num, while a cyclic
indirect descriptor is now rejected with -ELOOP.

summary: ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy

usx2y_urb_play_prepare() sums the packet lengths of a whole URB, copies
that many frames with a single wrap, and sizes each playback packet from
the capture packet's actual_length. Three things are unchecked: that the
URB fits in the ring buffer, that a packet fits in the playback
endpoint's maxpacksize, from which tmpbuf is allocated, and that
actual_length is a whole number of frames. The ISO descriptors take the
raw actual_length while transfer_buffer_length and the copies take
count * stride, so a packet that is not a multiple of the stride makes
the descriptors add up to more than the buffer, by up to stride - 1
bytes per packet.

Return -EPIPE, as the existing packet-size check does, when the URB is
larger than the buffer or a packet is larger than maxpacksize, and size
each descriptor from whole frames, so the descriptors add up to
transfer_buffer_length and each stays within maxpacksize. The buffer
case is prevented by the previous patch and this is the guard for it;
the other two depend only on the device.

The first case is reachable on the unpatched driver with ordinary
packets: on 7.3-rc7, a USB/IP device presenting the US-122 interface
layout and sending 48-frame packets, with a 100-frame playback buffer
(two 50-frame periods, inside the stock constraints), KASAN reports:

  BUG: KASAN: out-of-bounds in i_usx2y_urb_complete+0x79b/0x1ac0
  Read of size 18446744073709551280 at addr ffff88800e6b02e0 by task vhci_rx/80

With both patches, the same device and a 200-frame playback buffer is
refused at hw_params with EINVAL, and a 400-frame buffer plays for 30 s
with the position advancing inside the buffer, no KASAN report and
neither guard message. The maxpacksize check is not exercised: the
emulated device reports the same wMaxPacketSize on both endpoints.

The descriptor case is visible with capture packets of 195 bytes at
stride 4 (48 frames and 3 bytes): without this change the four
descriptors add up to 780 bytes for 768 bytes of data, and USB/IP's
completion check refuses the URB ("total length of iso packets 780 not
equal to actual length of buffer 768", -EPROTO), after which the driver
stops the streams. With this patch every descriptor is 192 bytes, the
descriptors add up to the data in every URB for 30 s, the position
advances inside the buffer and KASAN reports nothing. The 48-frame
playback run above is unchanged.

apparmor: fix a use-after-free in aa_lookupn_ns()

summary: ocfs2/dlm: serialize migration MLE cleanup on failure
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: serialize migration MLE cleanup on failure

A migration MLE has a base reference for the mastering answer and an
in-use reference held by dlm_migrate_lockres(). The finishing assertion
consumes the base reference, but migration failure drops it again
without checking whether the assertion already consumed it.

The target queues its migration worker before it acknowledges the
ALL_DONE packet, so its finishing assertion can be handled while the
sender still waits for the status. If the connection fails before the
status arrives, dlm_send_one_lockres() returns an error for a migration
that the target has already completed:

  Old-master sender                  Finishing assertion
  -----------------                  -------------------
  publish MLE; take in-use reference
  send ALL_DONE; wait for status
                                     take lookup reference
                                     unlink MLE
                                     put lookup and base references
  send returns a connection error
  put base reference again; free MLE
  put in-use reference; access freed MLE

dlm_assert_master_handler() holds dlm->spinlock from the MLE lookup to
the final puts, and it takes dlm->master_lock around the unlink and the
puts. Decide under the same locks: if the MLE is already unhashed, the
assertion consumed the base reference, so drop only the sender's in-use
reference. Otherwise unlink it before consuming the base reference so a
later assertion no longer finds it.

An assertion that got there first has also made the target the owner
and cleared DLM_LOCK_RES_MIGRATING. Treating the attempt as failed at
that point would leave the lockres owned by the target while this node
still holds the other nodes' locks and refmap bits, so it could neither
be purged nor migrated again. Finish our side as a completed migration
does instead: drop those locks under res->spinlock if the target still
owns the lockres, and recalculate its usage.

Use the same cleanup for the pre-send failure, the send failure and the
target-death failure paths. The sender's in-use reference keeps the MLE
alive until its final put outside the nested locks. Successful
migration retains its existing in-use-only put.

A target that has died cannot assert after the sender has seen its
death. The o2net node-down callback runs before the DLM one; it
disconnects the node and flushes the workqueue that runs the message
handlers, so an assertion already received has been handled by the time
the DLM removes the node from the domain map. A node that leaves the
domain cleanly sends its exit message only after its assertions have
been answered.

Two windows of the hand-over itself are left as they are: the handler
switches the owner and the sender drops the other nodes' locks moments
later, and an assertion from a live target that arrives after the
sender has given up still meets the owner check in the handler. Waiting
for the target before giving up would only stretch the first window
into the time in which recovery of the target can observe it.

summary: scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated

iscsi_parse_pr_out_transport_id() returns the ISID of a FORMAT CODE 01b
TransportID as a pointer into the PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT parameter list,
lowercased in place and never null-terminated.  spc4r37 Table 508 requires
the field to be null-terminated, but a non-conforming initiator can omit
the NULL; when the ISID ends at the end of the received buffer, the pointer
is not a C string.

The registration code still consumes it as one: strcmp() in
__core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg() and in the REGISTER AND MOVE path, and
snprintf("%s") in __core_scsi3_do_alloc_registration(), which also reads
its first 8 bytes unconditionally with get_unaligned_be64() - a NUL check
does not bound that read.

When the parameter list spans more than one page, transport_kmap_data_sg()
maps it with vmap(), and the over-read walks off the end of the mapping
into the vmalloc() guard page and oopses.  Reproduced with a PR OUT
REGISTER + SPEC_I_PT parameter list of exactly 8192 bytes whose final
TransportID carries a 12-byte ISID without a terminating NUL:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffc9000138c000
  RIP: 0010:strcmp+0xc/0x30
  Call Trace:
   __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg+0xd3/0x120 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port+0x8fc/0x13a0 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register+0x73c/0x900 [target_core_mod]
   ...
   iscsi_target_rx_thread+0xef/0x1d0 [iscsi_target_mod]

With a single-page parameter list the buffer is a kmap() direct mapping, so
the over-read continues into the physically adjacent page instead of
faulting.  snprintf("%s") then copies whatever follows the ISID in memory
into pr_reg_isid, and PR IN READ FULL STATUS reports the registration back
to any initiator, turning the over-read into an info leak of kernel heap
contents.  Reproduced with a 4096-byte parameter list whose last
TransportID ends at the end of the buffer with a 4-byte ISID and no NUL,
interleaved with I/O to populate adjacent pages: the READ FULL STATUS
response returned the ISID as "0xleak" followed by raw bytes that were not
part of the parameter list.  The snprintf() into
pr_reg_isid[PR_REG_ISID_LEN] caps the echoed ISID at 15 characters, so at
most 11 bytes past the buffer are leaked per command, but the PR OUT
command is not rate limited.

Any initiator that can send PR OUT to an iSCSI-exported LUN can trigger
either variant, including a guest via vhost-scsi.

Require 8 bytes to remain after the ",i,0x" separator, and a NUL inside the
rest of the descriptor, before the ISID pointer is returned.  REGISTER AND
MOVE fails with TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST; on SPEC_I_PT no target port
claims the malformed TransportID, and the command fails the same way.

summary: ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files

The OCFS2 debugfs file operation tables do not set owner. The
full debugfs proxy obtains real_fops with fops_get() at open and
keeps it until final release. Without an owner, this does not acquire
a reference to the module containing the table and its callbacks.
Removing the debugfs entries does not drain retained open files.

An open connected_nodes file can therefore outlive ocfs2_nodemanager
and make full_proxy_release() read real_fops->release from freed
module memory. Heming also reproduced the issue with fs_state and
asked for the other OCFS2 debugfs operation tables to be checked.

Set owner to THIS_MODULE in all eleven explicit debugfs operation
tables: five in ocfs2_nodemanager, four in ocfs2_dlm, and two in
ocfs2. The existing debugfs get/put pair then holds the appropriate
module until final release. Leave the open, read and release callbacks
unchanged. The blockcheck table already sets owner through
DEFINE_DEBUGFS_ATTRIBUTE(), so it needs no change.

The original controlled test used an unloadable OCFS2 module and
case-local probe filters without changing the candidate open, unload
or release logic. Closing a retained connected_nodes file after
normal unload produced:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfff804cfef
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  RIP: 0010:full_proxy_release+0xbf/0x190
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   __fput+0x39a/0xa60
   fput_close_sync+0xff/0x200
   __x64_sys_close+0x8c/0xf0
   do_syscall_64+0x114/0x620
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
   </TASK>
  Modules linked in: [last unloaded: ocfs2_nodemanager]

summary: media: usbtv: fix null-pointer dereference on disconnect
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: usbtv: fix null-pointer dereference on disconnect

A null-pointer dereference can occur in usb_make_path() when called from
usbtv_querycap() (and other ioctl handlers) during device disconnection.

Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
0xdffffc000000000a: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000050-0x0000000000000057]
RIP: 0010:usb_make_path include/linux/usb.h:985 [inline]
RIP: 0010:usbtv_querycap+0x9c/0x100
drivers/media/usb/usbtv/usbtv-video.c:612
...
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 v4l_querycap+0x236/0x470 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:1106
 __video_do_ioctl+0x8af/0xc70 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3133
 video_usercopy+0x860/0x1430 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3475
 v4l2_ioctl+0x18d/0x1e0 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-dev.c:366
 vfs_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:51 [inline]
 __do_sys_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:597 [inline]
 __se_sys_ioctl+0xfc/0x170 fs/ioctl.c:583
 do_syscall_x64 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63 [inline]
 do_syscall_64+0x174/0x580 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94

This happens due to a race condition between the USB device disconnect
routine (usbtv_disconnect()) and V4L2 ioctls. When the device is
disconnected, usbtv_disconnect() sets usbtv->udev = NULL without holding
the usbtv->v4l2_lock mutex. Concurrently, an ioctl handler like
usbtv_querycap() can be executing under the v4l2_lock and attempt to use
usbtv->udev, leading to a crash.

To fix this, move the usbtv->udev = NULL assignment into usbtv_video_free()
and protect it with mutex_lock(&usbtv->v4l2_lock). This ensures that no
non-queue ioctl handler can run concurrently with the pointer being
nullified. If an ioctl is already running, the mutex will block the
disconnect path until the ioctl finishes. If an ioctl is blocked waiting
for the lock, it will acquire it after the disconnect routine releases it,
but will then check video_is_registered() (which was cleared by
vb2_video_unregister_device()) and safely return -ENODEV.

Acquiring v4l2_lock after vb2_video_unregister_device() avoids
reintroducing a historical deadlock issue, and usbtv_audio_free() remains
safe as it is called before usbtv_video_free().

summary: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock()

The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options are copied from and
to user space while holding lock_sock(). A copy that faults or stalls,
e.g. on a userfaultfd or FUSE backed mapping, holds lock_sock() for its
whole duration.

raw_notify() and isotp_notify() take lock_sock() of a socket that is
bound to the vanishing device while holding RTNL. As the CAN_RAW
options can also be changed on a bound socket, a stalled copy can block
RTNL on an unregistration or namespace change of the bound device.
Before "can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock",
raw_setsockopt() even held RTNL itself during the copy. CAN_ISOTP only
copies its options for unbound sockets, which isotp_notify() skips
without taking lock_sock().

Keep the user space copies out of the locked sections: Check the option
name and length and copy the option values, including the CAN_RAW_FILTER
filters, to kernel memory before lock_sock(). raw_setsockopt_locked()
and isotp_setsockopt_locked() get the copied values directly and drop
their now redundant length checks and copies. As a side effect, a
failing copy can not leave partially overwritten options behind
anymore. In raw_getsockopt() duplicate the filters under lock_sock() and
copy them to user space after release_sock().

As the option name and length are now checked before lock_sock(), the
order of the checks in isotp_setsockopt() and accordingly the order of
the returned error values changes. This is in line with POSIX, which
does not define an order in which multiple error conditions are
detected and reported.

The generic SOL_SOCKET options in sk_setsockopt() are not affected by
this patch.

summary: batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client

When a ROAMING_ADV is received for an announced local client,
batadv_tt_local_mark_removed() sets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM, queues a
DEL|ROAM change and marks the entry as BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING. If the
client sends a frame again before the next TTVN commit,
batadv_tt_local_add_existing() only clears the PENDING flag and returns
early. The ADD cancels the queued DEL, but the entry keeps the ROAM flag:

* batadv_is_my_client() reports the client as not served by this node
* batadv_tt_local_client_is_roaming() reroutes unicast frames for it to
  the node which sent the ROAMING_ADV

The ROAM flag is only removed with the next frame of the client.

Since BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM is set together with BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING,
it has to be cleared also at the same time with BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING
when the client roamed back.

summary: ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs

An unprivileged user crashes the kernel by mounting overlayfs with the
volatile option.

A dentry that serves as the parent of a lookup must be a directory.
ovl_create_volatile_dirty() walks work/incompat/volatile/dirty by name,
and ovl_lookup_or_create() returns an existing entry whatever its type.
A file or a symlink that another task creates during the mount becomes
the parent of the next lookup, which calls a NULL ->lookup.

An unprivileged user mounted overlayfs with "volatile" in a user
namespace while a second process created a symlink named work/incompat,
and the mount task oopsed on a NULL ->lookup call.

Fix this by returning -ENOTDIR from ovl_lookup_or_create() when the
caller asked for a directory and the existing entry is a non-dir.

summary: ovl: set OVL_WHITEOUTS before publishing the upper dir
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set OVL_WHITEOUTS before publishing the upper dir

Listing a directory while it is copied up causes a use-after-free of
the readdir cache.

A merge directory must never be iterated as a real upper directory:
that mode frees the cache in OVL_I(inode)->cache without looking at
its refcount, while files opened in merged mode still use it.
ovl_copy_up_workdir() publishes the upper dentry before it sets
OVL_WHITEOUTS, and ovl_dir_open() samples both without a lock, so an
open between the two stores finds the upper directory and takes it
for a real one.

With a delay between the two stores, an unprivileged process that
listed a directory during its copy-up saw only "." and "..", and its
next getdents freed the readdir cache of another descriptor.

Fix this by setting OVL_WHITEOUTS before ovl_inode_update(), so that
ovl_dir_reset() agrees with ovl_dir_open(), and by testing
OVL_TYPE_MERGE() of the path type in ovl_dir_open(), so that an open
that observes the upper dentry never iterates a merge dir as a real
dir, regardless of the order in which it observes the flag.

[amir: test OVL_TYPE_MERGE() instead of smp_rmb() in ovl_dir_open()]

summary: ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the
reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry.
If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to
remove the volatile id.

Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before
either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops
its references first, the other request makes the final put through
ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first
session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed
memory.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 1030:
   __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd]

Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file
lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not
one made by another holder.

Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path,
before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the
request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which
holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup
is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

summary: mptcp: hold MP_JOIN msk ref when cloning reqsk
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: hold MP_JOIN msk ref when cloning reqsk

TCP request migration clones pending request sockets with
inet_reqsk_clone().  For MPTCP MP_JOIN requests this byte-copies
subflow_req->msk, but the clone does not own a reference.

The original and cloned requests can consequently drop the same msk
reference, leaving one request with a dangling pointer.  This manifests as
a KASAN slab-use-after-free in subflow_req_destructor():

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in subflow_req_destructor (net/mptcp/subflow.c:45)
  Write of size 4 at addr ff1100010e008d40 by task swapper/0/0
  CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 7.2.0-rc5-00353-gc27e36054537 #10 PREEMPT(full)

  Call Trace:
   subflow_req_destructor (net/mptcp/subflow.c:45)
   subflow_v4_req_destructor (net/mptcp/subflow.c:694)
   __reqsk_free (net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:906)
   reqsk_timer_handler (include/net/request_sock.h:137 net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:1147)

  Allocated by task 10014:
   sk_prot_alloc (net/core/sock.c:2246)
   sk_clone (net/core/sock.c:2488)
   mptcp_sk_clone_init (include/net/sock.h:1848 net/mptcp/protocol.c:3564)
   subflow_syn_recv_sock (net/mptcp/subflow.c:883)
   tcp_check_req (net/ipv4/tcp_minisocks.c:934)

  Freed by task 0:
   slab_free_after_rcu_debug (include/linux/kasan.h:235 mm/slub.c:2677 mm/slub.c:6439)
   rcu_core (kernel/rcu/tree.c:2645 kernel/rcu/tree.c:2897)

  Last potentially related work creation:
   kmem_cache_free (mm/slub.c:2638 mm/slub.c:6377 mm/slub.c:6504)
   __sk_destruct (net/core/sock.c:2289 net/core/sock.c:2391)
   sk_destruct (net/core/sock.c:2419)
   __sk_free (net/core/sock.c:2430)
   sk_free (net/core/sock.c:2441)
   mptcp_close (include/net/sock.h:2020 net/mptcp/protocol.c:3399)
   inet_release (net/ipv4/af_inet.c:442)

  The buggy address belongs to the cache MPTCP of size 2968
  The buggy address is 128 bytes inside a freed 2968-byte region

A non-NULL subflow_req->msk means that the request owns one reference. The
third ACK can concurrently transfer the original request reference to the
child and release it, so taking an unconditional hold on the copied pointer
is unsafe.

MPTCP sockets use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU and all current inet_reqsk_clone()
callers run in an RCU read-side critical section. Document and
lockdep-check that calling-context requirement.  Read the pointer from the
original request and acquire a reference only if it is still live.  Use
refcount_inc_not_zero_acquire() so the subsequent ownership validation
cannot be reordered before the try-get, then re-read the original request
to verify that it still owns the same msk. If either check fails, clear the
clone pointer; otherwise its normal destructor balances the new reference.
Mark the ownership-transfer store with WRITE_ONCE() to match the lockless
reads.

The following patch completes the clone fixup for MP_CAPABLE token
ownership. Both patches carry the same Fixes tag and are required for
stable backports.

summary: vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages

The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to the
request buffer during completion.  If a data-in command transfers less
than requested, part of a newly allocated bounce page can remain unwritten.

Allocate bounce pages with __GFP_ZERO so all bytes copied during completion
have a defined value.  This path is already the slow fallback for
misaligned I/O, so the added initialization cost is acceptable.

Found during an LLM-assisted source audit and validated with a QEMU/KVM
vhost-scsi target using misaligned data-in commands.

summary: smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race

Currently, init_cifs() calls cifs_proc_init() near the beginning of
the function, before INIT_LIST_HEAD, leading to a momentarily
uninitialized, but exposed, procfs. If a userspace process reads this
empty procfs, iterating over a zeroed list_head leads to a NULL
pointer dereference and a kernel oops/panic.

For example, if a delay is added between cifs_proc_init() and
INIT_LIST_HEAD, and a userspace process is polling
/proc/fs/cifs/DebugData, the following oops occurs:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000608
Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP PTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 3477 Comm: cat Not tainted
7.3.0-02212-g4df4d2a577db-dirty #6 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:cifs_debug_data_proc_show+0x103/0xd80 [cifs]
Call Trace:
<TASK>
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 seq_read_iter+0x183/0x400
 proc_reg_read_iter+0x62/0x90
 copy_splice_read+0x215/0x310
 splice_file_to_pipe+0xec/0x1c0
 do_splice+0x4b8/0x780
 __se_sys_splice+0x18f/0x250
 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x330
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
</TASK>

Fix this by moving cifs_proc_init() down in init_cifs(), ensuring it runs
only after all internal lists, locks, counters, and workqueues are fully
ready, but before registering the filesystem. Update the error cleanup
ladder and exit_cifs() to maintain proper LIFO order.

summary: mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after
unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH.  Both paths put back the isolated folio,
then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common
try_to_unmap_flush().

The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is
released.  Another collapse can replace and free it.  With its PTEs
already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB
batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs.  A CPU can
therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio.  This has been
reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.

Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still
held.  The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on
both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

summary: KEYS: encrypted: fix integer overflow of datablob_len
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KEYS: encrypted: fix integer overflow of datablob_len

encrypted_key_alloc() stores datablob_len in a u16. It is computed from
multiple string and payload lengths. If the result exceeds U16_MAX, the
assignment truncates the allocation size. KASAN reports a 32760-byte
slab-out-of-bounds write when __ekey_init() copies the master key
description into the undersized buffer.

The total payload length stored in key->datalen is also a u16. Use
check_add_overflow() to reject values that do not fit either destination,
and use kzalloc_flex() for the flexible-array allocation.

summary: iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure

viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_OK before populating the event
virtqueue and registering the IOMMU device in sysfs.  viommu_fill_evtq()
hands the device a set of device-writable buffers through
virtqueue_add_inbuf(), so from that point on the device may write into
them and into the rings.

If either step fails, the error path deletes the virtqueues without
resetting the device first.  The event buffers are allocated with
devm_kmalloc_array() and are released as probe unwinds, so the device can
go on writing to memory that has been freed.

Reset the device before deleting the virtqueues, the way viommu_remove()
already does.

summary: mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split

A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF after
shmem_undo_range() has handled the boundary folios. If splitting that
folio fails, truncate_inode_partial_folio() retains it when it is dirty.
The final scan then repeatedly finds it because it restarts from an
unchanged start.

Truncation keeps the inode lock and ignores fatal signals while looping.
A concurrent unlink() can then block other directory operations while
holding the directory lock and waiting for the file's lock.

Advance start past the retained folio, whose truncated part has already
been zeroed. Do not move start backwards if the failed split has shrunk
the folio.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: split fixes, simplify descriptions, adjust comments ]

summary: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error

When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a non-blocking invalidation, the
interval invalidation started beforehand is left unfinished: the caller
skips mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end(). Subsequent interval notifier
operations can then wait forever.

The only in-tree trigger is nouveau SVM, which uses both notifier types
and rejects non-blocking invalidations. Reaping via the OOM reaper or
process_mrelease() can therefore leave the GPU fault worker stuck,
holding a reference that prevents the dying process's address space
and memory from being freed.

End the interval invalidation when an ordinary notifier fails a
non-blocking invalidation, like mn_itree_invalidate() already does when
an interval notifier fails. Make that handling clearer in the
documentation of mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start_nonblock().

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: simplify description, update function doc ]

summary: net: extend IPv6 exthdr detection of tunneled packets
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: extend IPv6 exthdr detection of tunneled packets

Commit c4336a07eb6b ("net: correctly handle tunneled traffic on IPV6_CSUM
GSO fallback") split skb_gso_has_extension_hdr() into mutually exclusive
branches on skb->encapsulation. This did not yet address all paths:

1. With skb->encapsulation set, the outer header is not checked. IPv6
   tunnels such as ip6_gre and ip6_tunnel add an outer Destination
   Options header by default (encap_limit). Their GSO packets skip
   software GSO, then skb_csum_hwoffload_help() sees the outer extension
   header and calls skb_checksum_help() on the GSO skb, which warns and
   drops it.

2. Tunnels over IPv6 without an outer transport header, such as
   ip6_tunnel, leave skb->transport_header at the inner transport
   header. skb_network_header_len() then spans the outer IPv6, tunnel
   and inner IP headers, a false positive.

3. UDP tunnels without an inner network header, such as SCTP-in-UDP or
   PSP, have no inner IPv6 header to check. Decide on the outer header
   alone.

4. Directly dereferencing inner_ip_hdr(skb)->version without
   skb_header_pointer() is unsafe.

Instead, check ipv6_ext_hdr(nexthdr) on the outer IPv6 header and, if
set, on the inner IPv6 header. Read the headers with skb_header_pointer().
Keep the skb_network_header_len() check when !skb->encapsulation to also
catch encapsulated packets without skb->encapsulation (e.g., virtio).

Use the same helper in skb_csum_hwoffload_help(). Its open coded test
has the false positive of (2) and ignores the inner header.

Background: checksum offload of tunneled packets invariants:

Non-GSO skb:
- If the inner packet is CHECKSUM_PARTIAL, Local Checksum Offload computes
  the outer checksum in software and the device offloads only the inner L4
  checksum.
- If the inner packet is CHECKSUM_NONE (e.g., SCTP-in-UDP, ESP-in-UDP,
  Remote Checksum Offload), the device offloads the outer UDP or GRE
  checksum instead.

GSO skb:
- A device with NETIF_F_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL_CSUM or NETIF_F_GSO_GRE_CSUM
  computes both inner and outer checksums per segment.
  The outer checksum is seeded with only the pseudo-header checksum.

A NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM device must parse through the outer headers to
reach the inner ones.

summary: Bluetooth: hci_core: Fix race condition during device registration
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: hci_core: Fix race condition during device registration

In hci_register_dev(), the power_on work item is queued to
hdev->req_workqueue before initializing hdev->adv_monitors_idr and
registering the MSFT extension via msft_register(). For devices marked with
quirks such as HCI_QUIRK_RAW_DEVICE, the HCI_UNCONFIGURED flag is set on
the device. When the power_on work item runs concurrently on another CPU,
hci_power_on() detects that the device is unconfigured and immediately
invokes hci_dev_do_close(), which calls msft_do_close().

Concurrently, msft_register() allocates the msft structure and exposes it
to hdev->msft_data prior to calling mutex_init(&msft->filter_lock). If
msft_do_close() executes while hdev->msft_data is already assigned but the
mutex has not yet been initialized, mutex_lock(&msft->filter_lock) operates
on an uninitialized mutex, triggering a DEBUG_LOCKS warning:

DEBUG_LOCKS_WARN_ON(lock->magic != lock)
WARNING: kernel/locking/mutex.c:625 at __mutex_lock_common
kernel/locking/mutex.c:625 [inline]
WARNING: kernel/locking/mutex.c:625 at __mutex_lock+0x12d8/0x1550
kernel/locking/mutex.c:821
...
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 msft_do_close+0x308/0x7b0 net/bluetooth/msft.c:693
 hci_dev_close_sync+0x86b/0x10a0 net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c:5522
 hci_dev_do_close net/bluetooth/hci_core.c:499 [inline]
 hci_power_on+0x32c/0x750 net/bluetooth/hci_core.c:937
 process_one_work kernel/workqueue.c:3322 [inline]
 process_scheduled_works+0xa8e/0x14e0 kernel/workqueue.c:3405
 worker_thread+0x92d/0xe10 kernel/workqueue.c:3486
 kthread+0x388/0x470 kernel/kthread.c:436

 </TASK>

Fix this by moving the queue_work() call in hci_register_dev() to after
